findings.statement: JAK-STAT pathway activity is increased in inflamed UC mucosa in all eight cohorts (cohorts up [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=8]), with no cohort decreasing; this supports the already-approved JAK inhibitor class but is a broad signal shared with other pathways.

TNFa and NFkB pathway activity rise in every cohort, with the strongest t in GSE206285 (t [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=20.07]). This is the most uniform signal in the data and corresponds to the drug-targeted TNF axis, so it is a validation of the method more than a new lead.

STAT3 is among the strongest inferred transcription-factor activities, increased in all eight cohorts (GSE206285 t [type=tf_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; per_cohort.GSE206285.t=24.0]). The AP1 complex is also up in all eight cohorts. These are inferred from target genes, not from the factors' own mRNA, and reflect broad cytokine signalling (the IL6 family, IL23 and JAK).

Negative result: p53 and Androgen pathways do not behave consistently. p53 is decreased in only a minority of cohorts (cohorts down [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_down=3]) and is not significant in the rest; Androgen has opposite signs across cohorts. Neither should be called a UC-wide pathway.

WNT pathway activity is up in most cohorts (cohorts up [type=pathway_activity; source=ANALYSIS:pathways; cohorts_up=7]); one cohort (GSE73661) is not significant. Hypoxia is up in all eight. Both are non-drug-class-specific tissue-response signals, so they rank below specific circuits.

CXCR2 leads the convergence ranking, with meta-analysis log2FC [gene=CXCR2; type=expression_meta; source=DATASET:META; layer=rna; log2fc=2.814], same direction in all eight cohorts, genetic association and clinical-stage antagonists (reparixin, navarixin, ladarixin, SX-682). It is not yet an established UC drug target.

CXCR2 is a neutrophil receptor: in Gubatan 2026 neutrophil states make most of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts (Neutrophil, Neutrophil OSM, Neutrophil PADI4 lead), whereas Smillie 2019, which captured no neutrophils, shows only sparse T/NK signal and did not replicate. Its rise therefore reflects neutrophil infiltration, not a change in epithelial or stromal cells.

CXCL8 is made mainly by neutrophils in inflamed mucosa in the neutrophil-containing dataset (neutrophil share [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]); in the dataset without neutrophils macrophages appear to be the main source, so the apparent cell of origin depends on which cells were captured.

Leading CXCL8 circuit: CXCL8 from Neutrophil CXCR4 to ACKR1 endothelial cells has inflamed score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_inflamed=7870.993]. ACKR1 is an atypical chemokine receptor that presents chemokine, so this suggests endothelial neutrophil recruitment. The score is co-expression, not proof of signalling.

CXCL8 also acts neutrophil-to-neutrophil: Neutrophil CXCR4 to CXCR2 on Neutrophil has log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=2.755] versus uninflamed mucosa, a self-amplifying recruitment loop. No ligand-receptor pair with a fibroblast receiver appeared among the top CXCL8 pairs.

Weak circuit: OSM from Neutrophil OSM to IL6ST on LP fibroblasts is low in score and decreases in inflamed mucosa (log2 change [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; log2_change=-0.709]). Neutrophil PADI4 to LP fibroblast appears only in inflamed tissue, but at a low score. OSM sits well below the leading genes in the biomarker profile and outside the convergence top, with no drugs and no genetics. The neutrophil OSM to fibroblast circuit is thus not supported as a leading one.

IL1B pairs in the single-cell data are with IL1R2 (a decoy receptor) on neutrophil states, sent by monocyte-derived macrophages and neutrophils; the Neutrophil receiver pair has non-inflamed score [type=cell_communication; source=ANALYSIS:communication; score_noninflamed=0], so its log2 change is not finite and should not be read as a magnitude. IL1B has an approved drug (canakinumab) but not in UC.

TREM1 is near the top of the convergence ranking, up in all eight cohorts, with nangibotide (mid-stage clinical) as the only drug, but no ligand-receptor pair passes expression thresholds in the single-cell data, so sender and receiver cells cannot be assigned. It is an untargeted-in-UC candidate with unresolved circuit.

caveats: Pathway and TF activities are inferred from target genes in bulk biopsies and are broad: inflamed mucosa activates many pathways together, so cohort count alone does not identify a cause.
Ligand-receptor scores are co-expression (ligand mean x receptor mean), not proof of signalling; one single-cell dataset only, with few samples.
Cell-of-origin depends on whether neutrophils were captured (Gubatan 2026 yes, Smillie 2019 no).
Established drug classes (TNF, JAK-STAT, IL-23, integrins) were not individually queried for circuits; JAK-STAT and TNFa pathway signals are consistent with them.
Pathway-level data do not separate tissue change from infiltrating-cell composition.
